children: Anthropic
, which is in the process of going public, could reach a staggering $685B in revenue by 2030, Goldman Sachs analysts said, according to Bloomberg.
Enterprise sales could reach $586B, while non-enterprise sales could approach $100B, the news outlet added, citing a person familiar with the estimates.
Goldman Sachs
is the lead underwriter on the initial public offering. Morgan Stanley
is also one of the top underwriters on the offering.

Wall Street analysts have generally not issued research reports on companies before they go public, making the revenue target for 2030 somewhat unusual. However, it has happened in the past, including most
with SpaceX
Anthropic and Goldman Sachs did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

Anthropic is attempting to raise up to $64.4B in its IPO, with shares priced between $70 and $78 apiece, according to an updated version of its S-1 document it filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on
The company has also received commitments from major tech companies, including AMD
, Broadcom
, Google
, Micron Technology
, Microsoft
, NVIDIA
, and TSMC Partners to purchase a combined $26B of its Class N common stock through a private placement. The investors have agreed to buy the shares at a price equal to the IPO price.

Led by CEO Dario Amodei, Anthropic is offering 801.4M shares of Class A common stock, while existing investors are selling an additional 23.6M shares. Additionally, the firm will grant underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 123.75M additional shares at the IPO price, less underwriting discounts and commissions.
At the top end of the IPO price range, Anthropic would command a valuation of approximately $1T, based on the shares outstanding disclosed in the filing.
Anthropic

its initial public offering documents earlier this month, providing a look at its third quarter results. Revenue for the third quarter surged 1,127% year-over-year and 47% sequentially to $17B, with nine-month revenue totaling $33.2B. Operating loss for the period was $567M, compared to a $974M profit in the second quarter. Its net loss for the quarter was $23.3B, largely due to an accounting issue. Adjusted operating margin during the period was 15%, down from 19% in the second quarter.
Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT."
